name: ShaderScene
label: Shader scene
description: A WebGL2 scene, from a night horizon to a spiral galaxy or one of your own in GLSL, in the theme's field colours, with fades, vignette and grain.

props.name: scene
props.description:
The scene to paint: one of the library's by id, or a scene of your own as
a `ShaderSceneSource` (its colour roles, its settings and the GLSL that
paints it). The library's are `horizon`, a planet's limb at night, `rift`, a glowing tear, `glyphs`, soft light printed in type, `prism`, beams of light split into a spectrum, `meteors`, a shower over a planet's edge, `waves`, a rolling sea of points, `highway`, a straight highway at night drawn in light trails, `aurora`, ribbons of colour round a void, `ocean`, open water from above with sea life drawn in type, turquoise on a light page and moonlit on a dark one, `sky`, cloud massed overhead and burning with a low sun, a golden hour on a light page and the last of a sunset under a night sky on a dark one, and `galaxy`, a spiral galaxy seen at a slant, deep in a field of stars. A scene of your own is compared by content, so
an object written inline rebuilds nothing until what it says changes.

props.name: params
props.description:
The scene's settings, merged over its defaults (`SHADER_SCENES` lists each
library scene's keys and ranges; your own scene declares its own), so
passing one changes one thing. Changing them
never rebuilds the GL state.

props.name: passes
props.description:
The finishing passes (`scrim`, `vignette`, `fadeTop`, `fadeBottom`,
`grain`), each merged over its defaults.

props.name: speed
props.description: Scene seconds per second: how fast it moves. 0 holds it still.

props.name: liveRef
props.description:
A ref the scene reads every frame in place of `params`, `passes` and
`speed`, for a host that tunes it by drag: writing the ref moves the
scene and renders nothing. Empty falls back to the props.

props.name: enabled
props.description:
False never starts WebGL and reports `unavailable`, painting nothing:
the kill switch, as on ShaderField.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description:
Called whenever the status changes. Drive a fallback from this, or lay
one under the scene: it paints nothing until it is `active`, so what
shows while it is pending or cannot run is the caller's design
decision.

props.name: onError
props.description:
Called with the compiler's log when the scene's GLSL fails to compile or
link, for a scene of your own. Its line numbers count from the first
line of the scene's `glsl`, written `1:<line>`. The status becomes
`unavailable` as well, and the log still reaches the console. Replaces
the native `onError` attribute, which a scene's root never fires.

ShaderSceneId.description: The scenes the library ships, picked by id.

ShaderSceneParamSpec.description: One numeric setting of a scene, drawn as a slider by a host that offers controls.

ShaderScenePassSetting.description: One finishing pass's setting: whether it runs, and its own settings.

ShaderSceneSource.description:
A scene of your own, as ShaderScene's `scene` prop takes it: the colour
roles it reads, its settings, and the GLSL that paints it. Hold it at
module scope or pass it inline; the program is rebuilt only when its
content changes.

ShaderSceneStatus.description:
How the scene resolved, the same three states ShaderField reports.
`pending` while the GL context comes up (bounded by a watchdog), `active`
once a frame has painted, `unavailable` when it is disabled, WebGL2
cannot run it or its context is lost (it returns to `active` when the
context comes back, or after it rebuilds on a fresh canvas once it is
near the screen, passing through `pending`).

Values.description: What the canvas reads every frame. A ref holds it, so a drag never renders.
